content.title: About
content.content: Apple juice 100% is made from selected apple varieties grown without pesticides. It is fortified with calcium (4081 mg/L) to support bone health. The juice contains no added sugar, colourings or preservatives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Apple juice is a traditional beverage in many cultures and is often used in cooking.
The added calcium helps meet daily mineral needs, especially for children and those with higher requirements.
The juice retains most of the vitamin C naturally present in fresh apples.
When stored properly, the juice can keep its flavor and nutritional value for up to 12 months.
Apple juice is frequently used in baby foods as a base for purees and drinks.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Fortified calcium contributes to stronger bones and may reduce the risk of osteoporosis.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The juice contains no added sugar, making it suitable for those monitoring glucose levels.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Composed mainly of water, it helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Apple allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to apple juice.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, natural fruit sugars are present and should be considered by diabetics.

items.title: Shelf life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the juice can quickly lose freshness and become a medium for microbial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink it chilled as a refreshing beverage, add to smoothies, baby cereals, or use as a base for sauces and marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Peaches are juicy fruits of the peach tree (Prunus persica) grown in warm regions worldwide. Frozen peaches retain their sweet aroma, tender flesh, and bright color, making them convenient for year‑round culinary use.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peach is a close relative of almond, plum and cherry, all belonging to the Rosaceae family.
Peaches were first cultivated in China more than 4,000 years ago.
Peach skin contains antioxidants such as vitamin C and carotenoids.
Japan celebrates a "Peach Festival" to mark the beginning of the harvest season.
Frozen peaches are often used in desserts, smoothies and sauces because they retain most of their nutrients.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis, important for skin and blood vessels.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain electrolyte balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Peaches are low in calories, making them a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peaches, ranging from itching to swelling or hives.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Peaches are naturally sweet; people with diabetes should consider their glycemic impact.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Improper handling can lead to pesticide residues on frozen fruit; choose products from reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen peaches can be added to smoothies, yogurts, oatmeal, baked goods, sauces and ice cream. They also work well as pie fillings or a refreshing dessert after thawing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store frozen peaches in an airtight bag at –18 °C. After thawing, consume within 1–2 days and do not keep at room temperature for more than 4 hours.

puerto-rican-seasoning-without-ham-and-t.title: Puerto Rican Seasoning without Ham and Tomato Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Puerto Rican Seasoning without Ham and Tomato Sauce is a fragrant spice blend that reflects the culinary traditions of Puerto Rico. It contains dried peppers, garlic, oregano, cumin, coriander, onion powder and aromatics, but no ham or tomato sauce, making it suitable for vegetarians and those avoiding meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Puerto Rican cuisine blends Spanish, African and Indian influences, which are reflected in this seasoning.
The blend is commonly used with rice, beans, seafood and sautéed vegetables.
Without tomato sauce, it is more versatile – it can be added to sauces, marinades, and even dough for bread.
The mixture is stored in an airtight package to preserve aroma and flavor for several months.
The original recipe sometimes includes a pinch of sugar to balance the heat.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Contains turmeric and paprika, which have antioxidant properties that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cumin and coriander promote bile production and improve digestive function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Unlike ready-made sauces, this dry seasoning adds virtually no fat or calories.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides small amounts of vitamins B6 and B9, important for metabolism.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory effect
items.content: Oregano and garlic powder may offer mild anti‑inflammatory benefits.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pepper, garlic or oregano.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: The blend can be hot; people with sensitive stomachs should use it sparingly.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain versions add salt; check the label if you need to limit sodium.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: High amounts of turmeric may affect the action of anticoagulant drugs.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Sprinkle the seasoning on roasted vegetables, add it to marinades for chicken or fish, mix it into rice, beans, potatoes, or use it in soups and sauces. For a milder flavor, start with 1‑2 teaspoons per 500 g of food.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the seasoning in a tightly sealed container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage, refrigerate to preserve aroma. Prevent moisture from entering, as it can cause clumping.

content.title: About
content.content: Rice, fried, with pork is a classic Asian dish consisting of cooked rice stir‑fried with pieces of pork, vegetables and seasonings. The dish offers a savory aroma, balancing the mild sweetness of rice with the rich, slightly salty flavor of pork.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is popular in China, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam, each region adding its own signature spices.
Traditionally the rice is stir‑fried in a wok over high heat, giving it a light, crispy texture.
Soy sauce, sesame oil and ginger are common ingredients that deepen the flavor.
Some variations include pineapple for a subtle tangy note.
Leftover rice from the previous day is often used because drier rice holds flavor and texture better.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides steady energy by slowly releasing glucose into the bloodstream.

items.title: Protein from pork
items.content: Pork supplies all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, zinc and phosphorus are present, contributing to blood health and bone strength.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Ginger, garlic and soy sauce provide antioxidant compounds that help protect cells.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce and added seasonings can raise salt intake, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Pork fat
items.content: Some cuts of pork are high in saturated fat; choosing lean cuts is recommended.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: People allergic to soy should substitute soy sauce with a suitable alternative.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked pork may harbor pathogens; ensure the meat reaches an internal temperature of 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or side. It pairs well with a fresh vegetable salad, pickled cucumbers or chopped herbs. For a lighter version, use whole‑grain rice and lean pork pieces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat thoroughly until steaming to prevent bacterial growth.

strawberry-beverage-powder-dry-mix-not-r.title: Strawberry Beverage Powder, Dry Mix, Not Reconstituted

content.title: About
content.content: Strawberry beverage powder is a concentrated dry mix designed to create a flavorful strawberry drink without adding water. The powder contains dried strawberry extracts, sugar, flavorings, and stabilizers, delivering a rich taste and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The powder retains over 90 % of the vitamin C found in fresh strawberries thanks to low‑temperature drying.
Being dry, it is easy to store and transport and does not require refrigeration.
Natural strawberry aroma is often enhanced with natural essential oils rather than artificial flavors.
The mix can be used not only for drinks but also in baking, desserts, and yogurts as a flavoring agent.
Sugar levels are adjusted for different markets, with low‑sugar versions available.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Strawberries contain polyphenols and anthocyanins that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Vitamin C preserved in the powder aids the immune system.

items.title: Low in calories when used moderately
items.content: A small serving provides a tasty drink without a large calorie load.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Some formulations are fortified with fiber to aid digestion.

items.title: Promotes skin health
items.content: Vitamin C and antioxidants support collagen synthesis, benefiting skin.

items.title: Strawberry allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to strawberries may react to the powder.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Certain versions contain high sugar levels, which may be unsuitable for diabetics.

items.title: Additive sensitivity
items.content: Stabilizers and flavorings can cause sensitivity in some people.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Excessive intake can lead to unnecessary calories and sugar.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix 1–2 teaspoons of powder with 200 ml of cold water and stir or shake until fully dissolved. The powder can also be added to smoothies, yogurt, oatmeal, or incorporated into cake and muffin batters for a strawberry flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the powder in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Properly stored, it remains fresh for 12 months. After opening, use within 3 months for best quality.
